chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'if you have doubt' [65:4]. So he said: 'Whatever exceeds the month, then it is doubt.'

key_terms.ارتبتم: You have doubt — from the Quranic verse 65:4 about iddah of women with irregular cycles
key_terms.جاز الشهر: Exceeded the month — the threshold beyond which blood is classified as 'doubtful'
key_terms.ريبة: Doubt/suspicion — in jurisprudential context: bleeding of uncertain status beyond one month

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'doubt' in Quran 65:4 regarding menstruation?
ai.summary: Al-Halaby narrates that he asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the Quranic phrase 'if you have doubt' from Surah al-Talaq (65:4), which addresses the waiting period (iddah) for women whose menstruation has ceased. The Imam clarified that 'doubt' in this context refers to any blood flow that extends beyond a full month, since a woman's normal menstrual cycle does not exceed thirty days. This ruling helped early Muslim communities legally distinguish irregular bleeding (istihadha) from confirmed menstruation (haydi).
